key_insight: The EHR-integrated GenAI tool (iHGR) was more sensitive for VTE risk stratification than checklist-based order sets and slightly better than clinician-judgment ordering, though with lower specificity than the checklist approach.
clinical_relevance: This suggests GenAI may help identify more inpatients who need thromboprophylaxis support, but it should complement—not replace—clinician review.
method: Multisite retrospective validation at Johns Hopkins Medicine
500 randomly sampled adult inpatient admissions, balanced by site and workflow period
Compared iHGR and clinician-selected order set classifications against physician-adjudicated chart review
evidence_signal: In the validation sample, iHGR achieved 81.8% sensitivity and 70.9% specificity versus the reference standard.
watch_item: False negatives were linked to missed narrative risk factors, highlighting the challenge of extracting clinically important details from free-text notes.
paper_title: Multisite Real-World Validation of an Electronic Health Record-Integrated Generative Artificial Intelligence Tool for Venous Thromboembolism Risk Stratification
